moduleTitle: Advanced Use Cases - Mobile-Specific TCPs for Execution Tuning
learningObjectives: Describe mobile-specific test configuration parameters that help optimize test execution.
Separate the TCPs that establish a connection from the ones that tune how a run behaves.
Distinguish scan preview/reset options from execution TCPs and driver-specific state handling.
Explain why TCP scoping matters once the same TestCases run in more than one environment.

elements.description: Documented mobile TCPs configure connection, target and execution behavior. TMAServer and DeviceName are connection/target examples; LiveView, ScreenFlow, ScrollToVisible and TapByCoordinates control other documented behavior. Type is a Mobile Scan selection, not a generic execution TCP listed in the mobile TCP table. Invalid values in either group can produce errors; failure timing is not a guaranteed classification.

elements.text: Treat these categories as an explanatory aid, not a rule that connection mistakes always fail immediately while all other mistakes remain silent. Inspect actual effective values and failure evidence.

bulletPoints: Use documented TCP names and values for the actual connection.
Behavior parameters can also produce explicit errors.

elements.title: The levers worth knowing
items: LiveView=True enables execution screenshots that update when the TestStep changes; local execution only. The Mobile Scan Run Live View checkbox is a separate interactive preview setting, not the execution screenshot cadence.

Reset application is a Mobile Scan checkbox that resets user settings/permissions and restarts an already open app. It is not a universal execution TCP; session reset behavior requires the actual driver/capabilities and validation.
OSVersion is documented for iOS simulators and Android version-based selection without an exact device ID.

ScreenFlow=True saves screenshots of Input TestStepValues and requires ScreenFlowPath; TapByCoordinates=True provides a documented tap fallback for {CLICK}. Scan platform/OS/type filters are not a universal TCP filter grammar.

elements.description: Establish the application, account and relevant backend state required by each test. A driver-specific application reset may be useful, but a scan checkbox does not certify execution reset, complete backend cleanup or independence of every subsequent test.

bulletPoints: Separate interactive scan preview from local execution screenshots.
Validate application and backend baselines; no universal reset TCP is established.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Scoping, and why it starts mattering here

elements.description: TCPs are supported on multiple Tosca objects, including the project root, relevant folders, TestCases, ExecutionLists and ExecutionEntries. Child objects inherit values and lower-level values can override them. Bundled configurations support reuse; inspect effective values for each environment rather than inventing a fixed Project → Configuration → environment hierarchy.

elements.text: For otherwise equivalent scenarios, reuse TestCases and maintain connection differences in supported configurations to reduce duplication. Different workflows or target capabilities may still require purposeful test variants.

bulletPoints: Children inherit TCPs; lower-level overrides affect their descendants.
Reuse equivalent scenarios with configuration; validate purposeful variants when workflows differ.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing scan preview with execution LiveView
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting continuous interactive video from an execution TCP on every connection.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Execution LiveView provides local screenshots on TestStep changes. Scan preview uses its own checkbox; choose evidence collection appropriate to the run.

examPitfalls.title: Treating the scan reset checkbox as complete test isolation
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming Reset application guarantees every execution clears all application and backend state.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: The checkbox applies to Mobile Scan. Validate the actual execution driver/capabilities and explicit application/account/backend prerequisites.

examPitfalls.title: Duplicating equivalent tests for connection differences
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Maintaining drifting copies only to change the target/server.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Reuse supported configurations for equivalent scenarios and inspect inherited/overridden values. Separate test variants only for actual workflow differences.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which statement correctly describes the scope of mobile configuration parameters?

options.text: There is no practical difference; both stop the run immediately.
They configure connection/target and documented behavior; errors can occur in either category.
Tuning TCPs can only be set at Project level.
Connection TCPs apply to Android only.

practiceQuiz.hint: Category alone does not guarantee when or how a failure appears.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use documented TCPs for connection, targets and behavior. Their categories do not guarantee immediate versus silent failures, and TCPs are supported on several object levels and platforms.

optionExplanations.A: Neither category is guaranteed to stop every run immediately.
optionExplanations.B: Both documented connection and behavior settings can produce errors.
optionExplanations.C: TCPs are supported on multiple object levels.
optionExplanations.D: Mobile connection parameters are not Android-only.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Logs confirm a test fails only after a prior run because an account’s application state was not restored to its required baseline. Which response addresses the established cause?

options.text: Restore and verify the required state using the actual supported setup/reset workflow.
TMAServer is missing its trailing slash.
OSVersion is set to a specific value.

practiceQuiz.hint: The scenario establishes state carry-over, not a URL or screenshot issue.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Restore and verify the specific required state. The Mobile Scan reset checkbox does not establish a universal execution reset or backend cleanup guarantee.

optionExplanations.A: Screenshot display does not restore the confirmed account baseline.
optionExplanations.B: This addresses the established state carry-over using supported setup.
optionExplanations.C: The evidence establishes state carry-over, not this URL defect.
optionExplanations.D: An OS version value does not restore the confirmed account baseline.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Equivalent mobile scenarios need different supported connection values in development and CI. Which approach reduces unnecessary duplication?

options.text: Maintain two copies of each TestCase, one per environment.
Keep one set of TestCases and express the difference through TCP scoping across configurations.
Re-scan the application separately for each environment.
Use image-based controls so the environment stops mattering.

practiceQuiz.hint: The scenarios are stated to be equivalent; inspect effective configuration values.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use supported configurations and TCP inheritance/overrides to reuse equivalent TestCases. This does not guarantee one workflow covers genuinely different target behavior.

optionExplanations.A: Equivalent scenarios need not be duplicated solely for connection values.
optionExplanations.B: Supported configurations and TCP overrides allow equivalent scenario reuse.
optionExplanations.C: Different connection values alone do not establish a need to re-scan.
optionExplanations.D: Image identification does not eliminate environment requirements.

quickRecap.value: Documented parameters configure targets/connections and behavior; Type is not a generic listed execution TCP.
Either category can fail explicitly; diagnose actual evidence.
Execution LiveView: local screenshots on TestStep changes. Scan preview: separate checkbox.
Reset application is a scan option; validate actual execution state handling and backend prerequisites.
Children inherit TCPs; lower-level overrides and reusable configurations support equivalent scenarios.
